Northumberland: England's Quiet Giant

Northumberland is England's most sparsely populated county, and it wears its emptiness like a badge of honour. Where other popular tourist areas struggle with congestion, Northumberland's roads remain blissfully quiet. The combination of Hadrian's Wall, a stunning coastline, dark sky reserves, and vast moorland makes this an exceptional motorcycle destination.

Hadrian's Wall Country

The B6318 Military Road is Northumberland's signature ride. Following the line of Hadrian's Wall across the Whin Sill escarpment, it's a rolling, atmospheric road with long views in every direction. Stop at Housesteads Fort for the best-preserved section of the wall, and Vindolanda for one of Britain's most important Roman archaeological sites.

The Coast

Northumberland's coast is a succession of sandy bays, castle headlands, and fishing villages. Bamburgh Castle, rising from a basalt outcrop above a vast beach, is one of England's most impressive castles. Holy Island (Lindisfarne) is accessible by tidal causeway — check crossing times carefully. The Farne Islands, visible from the coast, host one of Europe's largest seabird colonies.

Kielder and Dark Skies

Kielder Water and Forest is England's most remote area — the forest is vast, the reservoir enormous, and the village genuinely isolated. Kielder holds a Gold Tier Dark Sky Park designation — the skies here are the darkest in England. Visit on a clear night and the Milky Way is stunning. The ride through the North Tyne Valley to reach Kielder is excellent.

Northumberland delivers what many UK destinations promise but fail to provide — genuine emptiness. These roads see less traffic than most Highland routes, yet they're just two hours from Manchester.

Where to Stay

  • Hexham — Historic market town, excellent base for Hadrian's Wall. Good pubs and restaurants
  • Alnwick — Castle town (Hogwarts filming location), bookshops, and riverside walks
  • Wooler — Gateway to the Cheviot Hills, quiet and unspoilt
  • Seahouses — Fishing village, boat trips to the Farne Islands, excellent fish and chips

What to See

Beyond the wall and coast, Northumberland offers Cragside (the first house in the world lit by hydroelectric power, National Trust), Alnwick Garden (one of Europe's most ambitious new gardens), and the Cheviot Hills — a wild and empty mountain range on the Scottish border. Rothbury in the Coquet Valley is a charming market town worth a detour.

Practical Information

Fuel is available in the main towns but limited in rural areas, particularly around Kielder and the Cheviots. Accommodation ranges from luxury country houses to simple B&Bs and campsites. The county is accessible from Newcastle (30 minutes to the park), Edinburgh (90 minutes), and Leeds/Manchester (2.5 hours). Visit May-September for the best weather. faq.q: What is the best road to ride in Northumberland?
faq.a: The B6318 Military Road is Northumberland's signature ride, following the line of Hadrian's Wall across the Whin Sill escarpment with long views in every direction. Stop at Housesteads Fort for the best-preserved section of the wall and at Vindolanda for one of Britain's most important Roman archaeological sites.

faq.q: How do I visit Holy Island safely?
faq.a: Holy Island (Lindisfarne) is accessible by a tidal causeway, so you must check the published crossing times carefully before setting off. The causeway floods at high tide and vehicles are regularly caught out and stranded. Plan your visit around the safe crossing window and allow enough time to return before the tide comes back in.

faq.q: Where can I experience dark skies in Northumberland?
faq.a: Kielder Water and Forest is England's most remote area and holds a Gold Tier Dark Sky Park designation, giving the darkest skies in the country. Visit on a clear night and the Milky Way is stunning. The ride through the North Tyne Valley to reach Kielder is excellent, though there are no fuel stations out there.

faq.q: Where should I refuel in Northumberland?
faq.a: Fuel is available in the main towns such as Hexham, Alnwick, Morpeth and Wooler, but it is limited in rural areas, particularly around Kielder and the Cheviot Hills. Fill up before heading into these remote areas, as some roads see very little traffic and stations can be far apart.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Northumberland?
faq.a: Visit between May and September for the best weather. The county is accessible from Newcastle in around 30 minutes to the park boundary, Edinburgh in 90 minutes, and Leeds or Manchester in about 2.5 hours. The coast can be windy year-round, so pack layers even in summer.
